facts.statement: The land where the Spiclypeus specimen was found was purchased in 2000 by Bill D. Shipp, a nuclear physicist.
facts.quote: In 2000, Bill D. Shipp, a nuclear physicist, bought the Paradise Point Ranch near the town of Winifred, in Fergus County.

facts.statement: The Spiclypeus specimen was discovered on September 2005 by Bill D. Shipp on his ranch in Montana.
facts.quote: On their first trip during an afternoon in September 2005, Shipp found the Spiclypeus specimen on his land in Montana.

facts.statement: The excavation team secured all remaining bones of the specimen by 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, Small and his team managed to secure all remaining bones.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was sold to the Canadian Museum of Nature for $350,000 to cover the excavation costs.
facts.quote: The specimen was sold to the Canadian Museum of Nature for $350,000, covering Shipp's expenses.

facts.statement: The species Spiclypeus shipporum was first described and named in 2016 by a team including Jordan C. Mallon and Christopher J. Ott.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus contains a single species, S. shipporum, first described and named in 2016 by Jordan C. Mallon, Christopher J. Ott, Peter L. Larson, Edward M. Iuliano and David C. Evans.

facts.statement: The genus name Spiclypeus means "spike shield" and refers to the spike-like horn ossifications on the frill margin.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin spica, meaning "spike", and clypeus, meaning "shield", in reference to its unique frill ornamented by many large spike-like horn ossifications on its margin.

facts.statement: The only known specimen, holotype CMN 57081, is housed at the Canadian Museum of Nature in Ottawa.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus is known solely from the holotype CMN 57081 which is housed at the Canadian Museum of Nature in Ottawa, Ontario.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus lived between 76.24 and 75.21 million years ago in the lower Coal Ridge Member of the Judith River Formation.
facts.quote: It was collected from the lower Coal Ridge Member of the Campanian Judith River Formation several meters above the mid-Judith discontinuity, which dates it to between 76.24±0.18 and 75.21±0.12 million years ago.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is estimated to have been 4.5 to 6 meters long and weighed about three to four tonnes.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus has an estimated length of 4.5 - 6 m and a weight of about three to four tonnes.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is unique among chasmosaurines for having a wrinkled contact surface on the rear projection of the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus is unique among Chasmosaurinae in having a wrinkled nose bone contact on the side surface of the rear projection of the premaxilla.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is unique for a combination of traits including sideways-projecting brow horns, fused epiparietals at the base, and specific curling patterns of the front frill horns.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus is also unique in having the trait combination of eye-socket horncores that project to above and sideways, all six epiparietals (frill horns) that are fused at their base, first two epiparietals pairs that curl down the frill surface on its front side, and third epiparietal pair that points back and towards the mid-line of the frill.

facts.statement: The reconstructed skull of Spiclypeus is 167 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The skull has a reconstructed length of 167 centimetres.

facts.statement: The triangular nose horn of Spiclypeus measures 166 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: The triangular nose horn has a length of 166 millimetres.

facts.statement: The brow horns of Spiclypeus measure 228 millimeters on the left and 246 millimeters on the right.
facts.quote: The postorbital, or brow, horns are 228 (left) and 246 (right) millimetres long.

facts.statement: The frill of Spiclypeus is ornamented with a unique pattern of skin ossifications known as osteoderms.
facts.quote: The frill of Spiclypeus features a unique pattern of skin ossifications or osteoderms ornamenting its edge.

facts.statement: Large osteoderms at the rear corners of the frill span the suture between the squamosal and parietal bones, a feature called an epiparietosquamosal.
facts.quote: At each rear corner of the frill a very large osteoderm is present. As it spans the suture between the squamosal and the parietal, this has been called an epiparietosquamosal or "EPS".

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is classified within the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus was placed in the Chasmosaurinae by Mallon et al. (2016).

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Spiclypeus as a sister species to a clade containing Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops, rather than in the Triceratops branch.
facts.quote: It was part of the Chasmosaurus instead of the Triceratops branch, as a sister species of a clade formed by Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Spiclypeus, Ceratops montanus, and Pentaceratops aquilonius might represent a single species, though this cannot be confirmed due to fragmentary fossils.
facts.quote: However, it is morphologically similar to the dubious ceratopsid species Ceratops montanus from the Judith River Formation and the dubious chasmosaurine species Pentaceratops aquilonius from the Dinosaur Park Formation (located just over the Canada–United States border and close in age) and in fact all three might represent a single species, which cannot be conclusively tested due to the fragmentary nature of the type specimens of these species.

facts.statement: Fossils of Spiclypeus were found in the Judith River Formation in Montana, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos se hallaron en sedimentos de la Formación Río Judith, en Montana, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 76 million years ago in the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 76 millones de años, durante el Campaniense

facts.statement: Spiclypeus was a large ceratopsian estimated to be 4.5 to 6 meters long and weigh 3 to 4 tonnes.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus es un ceratopciano de tamaño grande con una longitud estimada de 4,5 a 6 metros y un peso de unas 3 a 4 toneladas.

facts.statement: The reconstructed skull length of Spiclypeus is 167 centimeters.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene una longitud reconstruida de 167 centímetros.

facts.statement: The triangular nasal horn of Spiclypeus measures 166 millimeters in length.
facts.quote: El cuerno nasal triangular tiene una longitud de 166 milímetros.

facts.statement: The postorbital or frontal horns of Spiclypeus measure 228 millimeters on the left and 246 millimeters on the right.
facts.quote: Los cuernos postorbitales, o frontales, miden 228 el de la izquierda y 246 el de la derecha milímetros de largo.

facts.statement: The frill of Spiclypeus features a unique pattern of skin ossifications or osteoderms adorning its edge.
facts.quote: El volante de Spiclypeus presenta un patrón único de osificaciones de la piel u osteodermos que adornan su borde.

facts.statement: Researchers concluded that parallel injuries on the frill were likely caused by intraspecific combat where an opponent's brow horns pierced the shield bone.
facts.quote: It was concluded that they were probably the result of intraspecific combat, the brow horns of an opponent having pierced the shield bone.

facts.statement: A severe infection affected the entire lower half of the left humerus, causing dysfunction in the joint surface due to a large abscess.
facts.quote: The entire lower half of the bone was diseased. Most of the lower joint surface must have been dysfunctional, a large abscess having largely eaten away the condyles.

facts.statement: The body reacted to the humerus infection by remodeling the bone, rotating the joint over 90 degrees from its normal orientation.
facts.quote: The bone had been reworked in reaction, rotating the joint over 90° from its normal orientation.

facts.statement: Extensive bone remodeling suggests the infection was not immediately lethal and may have been caused by a less virulent form of tuberculosis or fungus.
facts.quote: Extensive remodelling of the bone shows that the infection had not been immediately lethal and was perhaps the result of a less virulent tuberculosis or fungus.

facts.statement: The genus Spiclypeus was named by Mallon et al. in 2016.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Mallon et al., 2016

facts.statement: It is debated whether Spiclypeus, the dubious Ceratops montanus, and Pentaceratops aquilonius are distinct species or a single species, as conclusive proof is impossible due to the fragmentary nature of the type specimens.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, es morfológicamente similar a la especie de casmosaurino dudoso Ceratops montanus de la Formación Río Judith y a Pentaceratops aquilonius de la Formación Dinosaur Park, localizada justo sobre la frontera Canadá-Estados Unidos y de edad similar y de hecho estas tres formas podrían ser una sola especie, lo cual no puede ser probado concluyentemente debido a la naturaleza fragmentaria de los especímenes tipo de estos dinosaurios.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Spiclypeus was discovered in September 2005 on land owned by Bill D. Shipp in Montana.
facts.quote: En su primer viaje durante una tarde de septiembre de 2005, Shipp encontró el espécimen de Spiclypeus en su tierra en Montana.

facts.statement: Amateur paleontologist Joe Small was hired to excavate the Spiclypeus fossils after they were found.
facts.quote: Shipp luego contrató al paleontólogo aficionado Joe Small para excavar los fósiles.

facts.statement: Joe Small and his team recovered all remaining bones of the specimen by 2007.
facts.quote: En 2007, Small y su equipo lograron asegurar todos los huesos restantes.

facts.statement: The Spiclypeus holotype was sold to the Canadian Museum of Nature for $350,000 to cover excavation costs.
facts.quote: El espécimen se vendió al Museo Canadiense de la Naturaleza por 350.000 dólares, cubriendo los gastos de Shipp.

facts.statement: The genus Spiclypeus contains only one species, S. shipporum, which was formally described and named in 2016.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus solo contiene a una especie, S. shipporum, descrita y nombrada originalmente en 2016 por Jordan C. Mallon, Christopher J. Ott, Peter L. Larson, Edward M. Iuliano y David C. Evans.

facts.statement: The genus name Spiclypeus refers to the ornate frill featuring large, spine-like ossifications along its edge.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del latín spica, que significa "espina", y clypeus, que significa "escudo", en referencia a su característica gola ornamentada con varias osificaciones grandes en forma de cuernecillos espinosos en el borde de la misma.

facts.statement: The species name shipporum honors the original owners of the type specimen, Dr. Bill and Linda Shipp.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie, shipporum honra al Dr. Bill y a Linda Shipp, los propietarios originales del espécimen tipo, y a su familia.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is known only from the holotype specimen CMN 57081, which is housed at the Canadian Museum of Nature in Ottawa.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus es conocido exclusivamente a partir del espécimen holotipo CMN 57081 el cual es alojado en el Museo Canadiense de la Naturaleza en Ottawa, Ontario.

facts.statement: The fossil was collected near Winifred in Fergus County, Montana, from the Coal Ridge Member of the Judith River Formation dating between 76.24 and 75.21 million years ago.
facts.quote: Este fue recolectado, tras el descubrimiento por B.D. Shipp en septiembre de 2005, cerca del pueblo de Winifred, en el Condado de Fergus, en la zona inferior del Miembro Coal Ridge de la Formación Río Judith a varios metros por encima de la discontinuidad media de la Fm. Judith, la cual data de entre 76.24±0.18 a 75.21±0.12 millones de años.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus was classified in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae in 2016.
facts.quote: Spiclypeus fue situado en 2016 en la subfamilia Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is the sister species to a clade containing Kosmoceratops and Vagaceratops, rather than being closely related to Triceratops.
facts.quote: Formaba parte del linaje de Chasmosaurus en lugar de ser cercano al de Triceratops, siendo la especie hermana de un clado formado por Kosmoceratops y Vagaceratops.

facts.statement: The parent group of Spiclypeus is the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Chasmosaurinae

facts.statement: Spiclypeus belongs to the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Spiclypeus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Spiclypeus lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: The type specimen of Spiclypeus shows a significant infection on its frill, hypothesized by some to be an injury inflicted by a rival of the same species.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Spiclypeus parece haber tenido una significativa infección en su gola, la cual se ha considerado por algunos como una herida infligida por un rival de su misma especie.

facts.statement: Perforations in the frill of the Spiclypeus holotype are likely the result of intraspecific combat where an opponent's brow horns pierced the bone.
facts.quote: Se concluyó que probablemente eran el resultado de un combate intraespecífico, los cuernos de la frente de un oponente habían perforado el hueso del escudo.

facts.statement: A severe infection affected the lower half of the left humerus, rendering the joint largely dysfunctional due to a large abscess that destroyed the condyles.
facts.quote: Otra infección mucho más grave estaba presente en el húmero izquierdo. Toda la mitad inferior del hueso estaba enferma. La mayor parte de la superficie articular inferior debe haber sido disfuncional, un gran absceso que se había comido en gran parte los cóndilos.

facts.statement: Bone examination indicates the Spiclypeus specimen was a mature individual at least ten years old, lacking signs of rapid juvenile growth.
facts.quote: El examen de los huesos del espécimen también indica que corresponde a un individuo maduro, de al menos diez años de edad ya que no hay signos del crecimiento rápido asociado con los ceratopsios juveniles.

facts.statement: Analysis of growth lines in the femur indicates a minimum age of ten years for the holotype specimen.
facts.quote: Siete de estos LAG están presentes y probablemente un número mínimo de tres líneas haya sido ocultadas por procesos de crecimiento posteriores, lo que da como resultado una edad mínima estimada de diez años.
